subject.title: Design: Telegram isolated ingress holds per-chat lane for the entire agent turn — long turns block the group, then die at 25 min

question: Should Telegram isolated ingress release the per-chat/topic spool lane after durable handoff to session admission instead of after the full agent turn completes?
rationale: The source-level failure is clear, but the permanent fix chooses ownership for Telegram ordering, replay, timeout, and session steering semantics, which should be an explicit maintainer design decision before implementation.

options.title: Detach After Durable Handoff
options.body: Move lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable session handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

options.title: Keep Lane Ownership And Tune Timeout
options.body: Preserve one-handler-per-lane transport ownership and improve timeout/user feedback, accepting that mid-turn same-lane messages remain invisible to steering.

options.title: Split Follow-Ups First
options.body: Handle timeout visibility and progress feedback separately while leaving lane detachment as a larger design item.

recommendation.title: Detach After Durable Handoff
recommendation.body: Move lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable session handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and authored the related run-lifecycle work that exposed the next Telegram transport ownership gap.
